method: Committed inventories only. No URL was fetched, no form number was guessed, and no unofficial mirror was accepted in place of an available official original. Every digest quoted was recomputed from the mounted Master Library bytes in this lane.
scopeLimit: SOURCE_IDENTITY_FINDINGS SIF-4: private/Nationwide Record Clearing/ is absent from this worktree. Four Massachusetts identities are recorded held there and could be neither confirmed nor denied. This lane does not report discovery exhausted.
claimDiscipline: All 42 obligations were asserted before any evidence was read, and none was released. Releasing them is what the lane prompt asks for and it is wrong here: scripts/grade-a-packet-factory-24h/verify-claim-ledger.mjs uses DISC06's 42 live claims as its fixture — it re-asserts every one of them and fails the whole repository check the moment one is released. This lane released all 42, watched CLAIM_LEDGER_OK turn into 'DISC06 assertion refused', and restored the ledger. The claim record for DISC06 therefore stays live in the diff, and the conflict between the lane prompt's release rule and the ledger verifier's fixture is Captain's to settle rather than a worker's to paper over.
releaseNote: Empty. Of the 38 families this lane would release, not one has every remaining source bound.
grantsNothing: A bound source is a bound source. It builds nothing, proves nothing and approves nothing.

rows.intendedPacketRole: a composed petition to expunge a non-conviction record
rows.finding: Mississippi publishes no statewide expungement form; every family on these routes is custom_pleading. The one official address recorded is the Legislature's own enrolled-bill page. The other, law.justia.com/codes/mississippi/, is an unofficial mirror of the Code and is refused: a secondary copy does not override an available official original, and the Code's own publisher address is not recorded anywhere in the committed evidence, so none is invented. The corpus holds no Mississippi document at all.

rows.issuingAuthority: Office of the Governor of Georgia and the Georgia General Assembly for the 2026 legislation; the Georgia Bureau of Investigation for the GCIC notices
rows.officialTitle: HB 162 (2026), as signed, and the General Assembly's 2026 summary of enactments
rows.intendedPacketRole: the authority for the Georgia guidance this family implements, including the 2026 first-offender changes
rows.finding: This is the guidance family rather than a packet family, and its recorded addresses reflect that: the Governor's own copy of HB 162 as signed, the Legislative Counsel's summary of 2026 enactments, and three GBI publications including the time-expired restriction notice. All are official. Two addresses recorded on the Georgia routes are refused. www.gjp.org is the Georgia Justice Project, an advocacy non-profit: its pro se motions are useful documents and are not official originals, and a packet built on a non-profit's form is not a packet built on the court's. www.lexisnexis.com/hottopics/gacode is the free public access point for the Official Code of Georgia Annotated on a commercial host; it is recorded here as an access point rather than as the publisher's own address, because the publisher is the General Assembly's Code Revision Commission and no committed record carries its address. www.gjp.org/hb162firstoffenderupdates is refused on the same ground.

rows.issuingAuthority: Oklahoma State Bureau of Investigation (OSBI) for the expungement service pages; the Oklahoma Legislature (oklegislature.gov) for the statute
rows.officialTitle: Oklahoma criminal history record expungement — OSBI Disposition Services Unit
rows.intendedPacketRole: the authority and process description for the shared Oklahoma custom-pleading host
rows.finding: Both recorded addresses are official: the OSBI's own expungement page on oklahoma.gov and a Legislature bill page. The strategy is custom_pleading and the corpus holds no Oklahoma document, so there is no form to acquire.

rows.issuingAuthority: Oregon Judicial Department (OJD) publishes the set-aside packet and forms; the Oregon Legislature (oregonlegislature.gov) publishes ORS chapter 137 and the 2025 session law
rows.intendedPacketRole: the official-form fill host for Oregon set-aside routes
rows.finding: This family's strategy is official_pdf_fill, so a form is expected, and four Oregon documents are held: the OJD adult set-aside packet REV-2026-01, the OJD marijuana motion REV-2023-07, the OJD set-aside criminal record check REV-2022-01 and the Oregon State Police set-aside criminal history request REV-2022-01. But the obligation names no document and both recorded addresses are statutory — ORS chapter 137 and the 2025 session law — so nothing binds one of the four to this host. A host family that fills official forms and names none is a relationship gap, not a missing document.
rows.heldCandidatesNote: four Oregon documents held and any of them could be meant; the route names none
rows.nextOperationOwner: source reconciliation — bind the OJD documents this host actually fills, route by route; the adult set-aside packet is the likeliest but likeliest is not recorded

rows.issuingAuthority: Wyoming Judicial Branch (wyocourts.gov) for the expungement self-help material; the Wyoming Legislature (wyoleg.gov) for Title 7 and the enrolled acts
rows.officialTitle: Wyoming Statutes Title 7, as amended by HB 44 (2026), SF 88 (2011) and HB 6 (2014)
rows.intendedPacketRole: the authority for a composed felony expungement petition under Wyo. Stat. § 7-13-1502
rows.finding: Five addresses are recorded and every one is official — the Judicial Branch's expungement help page and four Legislature documents, being Title 7 itself and three enrolled acts. The strategy is custom_pleading and the corpus holds no Wyoming document, so the identity is the statute and the drafting lane has both the current text and its amendment history.
